title: Do Multilingual Large Language Models Mitigate Stereotype Bias?
findings: The study's general conclusion that multilingual models are less biased than monolingual ones does not consistently hold for the 'Religion' category. On the CrowS-Pairs benchmark, results were mixed, with the multilingual model showing less bias in German and French but more bias in English, Spanish, and Italian. On the BBQ benchmark, for the religion category, the multilingual model consistently showed higher magnitude bias scores (i.e., were more biased) than its monolingual counterparts across all five tested languages.
